title: What the World Hands Back
prompt: The System asked a question and tried to count with the answer. It broke. Find where.

config.symptom: TypeError — can only concatenate str (not "int") to str.

line_hints.0: Asking is fine. input() always succeeds — it is what it hands back that surprises people.
line_hints.2: Printing is innocent. It never gets the chance to run.

fixes.why: input() ALWAYS hands back a string, even when the traveller typed digits. '7' + 1 is meaningless until you say: read this as a number.
That runs — and gives '71'. You glued a character on the end instead of counting. Two strings joined is not arithmetic.
Python has no ++ at all. That is a different language's habit, and here it is simply a syntax error.

config.success: The world always answers in words. Turn them into numbers before you count with them.
